newsitem.title: USA: Transit to sell parcel delivery business.
newsitem.headline: Transit to sell parcel delivery business.

text.p: Transit Group Inc said Thursday it has signed a non-binding letter of intent to sell its parcel delivery business to privately held Western Parcel Express Inc.

Transit, formerly General Parcel Service Inc, said that under the proposed sale, Western Parcel would assume about $2.4 million in leases relating to vehicles and equipment for the parcel delivery business.
It also would assume all leases on remaining operating facilities, virtually completing Transit Group's transformation into a holding company for truckload carriers.

Transit's parcel delivery business accounted for substantially all of its $23.4 million in revenues for 1996 and the $5.1 million, or $1.48 per share, net loss reported for that year. "We are very pleased to announce another positive step in our efforts to reorient Transit Group to become a consolidator of truckload carriers," President and Chief Executive Philip Belyew said in a statement. "When completed, this transaction will remove what has been a serious drain on the company's resources and eliminate all debt relating to those operations effective June 30, 1997."
Transit said it expects to complete the sale during the third quarter of 1997 and will report a one-time loss of about $6 million on the disposition of this business.
